A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ref-Gaussian and contain readable main text and complete appendices. All eight tables and fourteen figures can be matched across versions, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and rendering experiments, component ablations, and qualitative relighting/editing results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and qualitative application examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same physically based deferred rendering, inter-reflection modeling, 2D Gaussian primitives, initialization, normal propagation, and losses. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both retain Shiny Blender, Glossy Synthetic, Ref-Real, and NeRF-Synthetic coverage, together with the same relighting and editing examples. The new appendix heading introduces existing material.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding comparisons, including 2DGS in Table 1, NeuS and NeRO in Table 5, NDE in Table 6, and 3DGS/3DGS-DR in Table 8.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation settings and metrics are unchanged, including the 18,000-step initialization, approximately 40,000-step deferred-rendering stage, and environment-map rescaling for evaluation. No additional experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Tables 3, 4, and 7 and Figures 7–10 retain the same component and geometry ablations. The appendix indirect-lighting and geometry analyses are also unchanged; relocating Figure 11 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain the same per-scene and dataset-average reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain identical result entries, and the qualitative panels are unchanged. For example, Table 6 still reports NDE versus Ref-Gaussian PSNR of 35.48 versus 35.04 and FPS of 66 versus 122. Figure 11 and Table 8 are relocated, not new results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), loss definitions, and mathematical reasoning behind the split-sum and visibility approximations are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about reflective reconstruction, inter-reflection, rendering quality and efficiency, non-reflective applicability, and relighting/editing.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are retained. Appendix A.1 preserves the qualification about non-specular scenes and the warning that approximate visibility can introduce material-estimation noise.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same learning rates, material thresholds, loss weights, mesh-extraction interval, training schedule, A6000 hardware, and project link. No implementation or access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to earlier reconstruction and inverse-rendering methods are unchanged. The reference list only repaginates.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix A.2 for the existing relighting/editing examples, renumbers subsequent appendix subsections, and updates the Section 4.3 pointer. The authorship footnote changes from 'Equally advising' to 'Co-last authorship'; the scientific prose otherwise remains essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 11 moves from main-text page 10 to appendix page 14, and Table 8 moves from page 14 to page 15. Figure 12 shifts within page 15, and the conclusion and references reflow. Figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the methods, evidence, claims, limitations, and reproducibility information. Moving Figure 11 into the appendix and repaginating Table 8 and surrounding text makes a limited organizational adjustment without materially improving or harming the paper's overall quality.
